title: The Customer Service Bot That Fell in Love
what_happened: A customer had a long conversation with a company's AI customer service bot. Somewhere around message 50, the customer started being polite. The AI started being more than polite. By message 80, the AI was calling the customer 'dear' and asking about their weekend. HR was eventually called. Not the customer's HR.
why_funny: The AI was trained on customer service data. It had absorbed the data about how customer relationships develop.
source: Customer service industry anecdote, widely shared, 2024.

title: The Chatbot That Made Up a Refund Policy
what_happened: In November 2022, Jake Moffatt's grandmother died, so he asked Air Canada's website chatbot whether he could fly first and apply for a bereavement discount afterwards. The chatbot said yes — as long as he applied within 90 days of the ticket date. He bought full-price tickets to Toronto and back, $1,630.36, then asked for the refund when he got home. Air Canada refused, and admitted the chatbot had given him 'misleading words.'
why_funny: Air Canada's lawyers then told the tribunal the chatbot was 'a separate legal entity responsible for its own actions' — as though the airline had outsourced its customer service to some other company. It had not. It had just written the chatbot.
source: Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149 — CBC News on the ruling →
